description: Check an EAS workflow file before it runs, the way eas workflow:validate does, without a checkout: the file as the project's repository has it at a ref (workflow and git_ref; EAS reads it from GitHub, as a dispatch would), or a file (path). Answers valid, the issues (YAML that does not parse, a needs: naming no job, and every problem EAS's own validator names, field by field), the jobs, and the build jobs a dispatch would spend credits on. Runs nothing, spends nothing. Never type or paste a file's base64 yourself: a retyped file can arrive changed. Give the path of a file in your workspace folders (the roots this client shares; without them /tmp/churn-qgyglw3_), or have a script that read the file send content_base64 with its sha256.

content_base64.description: Instead of path: the file's bytes as standard base64, only as a script that read the file wrote them, never typed. Needs sha256.

git_ref.description: With workflow: a branch ("main"), "refs/heads/<branch>", "refs/tags/<tag>" or a commit hash the repository already has.

path.description: Instead of workflow and git_ref, a workflow file: a file in your workspace folders (the roots this client shares with the server; without them /tmp/churn-qgyglw3_); a bare name is taken from the first. Links are refused.

project.description: The project: "@account/slug" (e.g. "@acme/my-app"), its slug, or its id. Leave it out when the token sees one project (list_projects).

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of the source file, as sha256sum prints it. Required with content_base64, checked with path.

workflow.description: With git_ref: the workflow file as the repository has it there, e.g. "ios-build.yml"; a file EAS has not run yet works too.

name: validate_workflow
title: Validate workflow
